units.translation: Thus Hermann. προσ-κείσεται [will be added] M, with the first sigma erased.
AN. You lie exposed. IS. Having slain
Is there no end of the contest set before you?
But now no end of toils is set before me
It was set before all to be deprived of their head
Do not care for me more than is sweet to me
Of a man holding a drawn sword there.
Περ [About] ἕτοιμος [ready] and πρόχειρος [at hand] from the excerpt. Photius p. 455, 16.
Let everyone make ready a sword with hilt drawn
But I too, with sword drawn, do not refuse to die
About ready and at hand from the excerpt. Photius p.
For I declare that the dead man fares better than these
restored from the apograph: προ [before] Ἀγβάτανα [Ecbatana] λιπών [having left].
having left the ancient Cissian citadel, they went
restored from the apograph: before Ecbatana having left

where the scholiast explains: πολλὰ προοιμιάζου [make many preambles], and in another scholium: μήτε προτέρα κατάρχου τοῦ λόγου μήτε ἀμειβομένη μακρολόγει [neither begin the speech first, nor, when answering, speak at length].
Do not be forward in speech or over-ready to talk
neither begin the speech first, nor, when answering, speak at length
being a prophetess of these things
Cypris, as the ancestress of the race

where in M προμήθειαν [forethought], but with 1 written above, i.e. προμηθίαν [forethought]. Both forms are correct, but the tragedians seem to have preferred προμηθία [forethought], which form in Sophocles and Euripides the meter everywhere either allows or demands: on which I have spoken in Thes., vol. 6 p. 1776.
And now, taking forethought for the land, I advise you to guard it
where M has προθυμεῖσθαι [to be eager]. Corrected from the note of the scholiast, who explains it by προνοεῖσθαι [to take forethought].
In taking forethought and daring, what penalty do you see present?
Prometheus, son of the Titan Iapetus
Doric form προμηθεύς [Prometheus], but with α written above, M. Where the meter demands προμαθίς [forethoughtful], which Hermann restored.
